coaching.coaching: Run a quick pre-mortem on unbounded growth risk of the persistent HLC-to-Jira-ID map: how could this plan fail?
coaching.subject: unbounded growth risk of the persistent HLC-to-Jira-ID map

metrics.claim_path: no-llm/no-network (structural; the fast claim check is a local HMAC verify)

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the RETIRE/cleanup lifecycle for the comment-ID map (e.g. it is retired with the binding record, or explicitly document that unbounded per-comment growth is acceptable and bounded by binding lifetime).
evidence: 'The map is change-gated, one fixed-shape entry per comment.'
Append-only semantics mean entries are only ever added, never removed.
No mention of eviction, pruning, or lifecycle retirement for the map across the plan.
findings.finding: The new persistent local_comment_key(HLC)→Jira-comment-ID map is append-only and grows one entry per comment forever, with no RETIRE/cleanup path defined; the plan does not address unbounded accumulation of map entries in binding state.
findings.location: Approach 1 / Scope binding_store.py — 'Persist a local_comment_key (HLC) → Jira comment ID map in binding state'
scenarios: A long-lived binding accumulates thousands of comment entries over its lifetime, growing binding state indefinitely.
A binding is deleted/retired but its comment map has no defined cleanup responsibility.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a sentence to Approach 1 clarifying the map is owned by and retired together with the binding record (so it cannot leak independently), or note an explicit bound/pruning rationale if growth is a concern.

evidence: Plan: 'already on the compiled entry at `reducer/_processors.py:349`' and Scope '`reducer/_processors.py` — HLC key (`:349`); `jira_comment_id` (`:354-356`)'

findings.finding: The plan's reference anchor for the load-bearing HLC-key premise points to a non-existent directory and wrong lines: it cites `reducer/_processors.py:349` (HLC timestamp) and `:354-356` (jira_comment_id) under `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/`, but that `reducer/` subdirectory does not exist — the file is `src/rebar/reducer/_processors.py`, and the relied-upon fields are at line 203 (`timestamp`) and 207-209 (`jira_comment_id`). Line 349 there is `_IMMUTABLE_EDIT_FIELDS`; 354-356 is the EDIT-processor docstring. The underlying PREMISE (compiled COMMENT entry carries the HLC `timestamp` and `jira_comment_id`) is TRUE, so this is a citation-accuracy defect, not a false premise — but it would send an implementer to a non-existent path.
scenarios: Implementer follows the cited path/lines to wire the local_comment_key and finds no comment code there
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the path with `src/rebar/reducer/_processors.py` and the lines with the COMMENT-processor block (~L200-218).

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Verify (via a read-only acli probe that inspects the LANDED comment body, not just exit code, or via the REST payload path) that `comment create --body <ADF JSON>` actually RENDERS as ADF rather than storing the JSON as plain text; retrieved prior art indicates the create surface only renders via `--body-adf`/`--body-file` and even those may show plain text — resolve this before flipping the codec.
evidence: Plan text: "--body accepts ADF ... acli jira workitem comment create --help documents '-b, --body string Comment body in plain text or Atlassian Document Format (ADF)' ... so --body json.dumps(to_wire(body)) is supported like --description"

Retrieved Atlassian Community forum (community.atlassian.com/forums/.../qaq-p/3171539, Jan 2026): the ADF-render path is `acli jira workitem comment update ... --body-adf /path/to/comment.adf.json` which 'renders bold, italic, lists ... perfectly'; the user asks whether there is a `--body-adf` for `comment create` 'that's not documented in the help menu' — implying create lacks a working inline-ADF path.

Retrieved same forum: `acli jira workitem comment create -k TICKET-123 --body-file comment.adf.json` -> 'Comment is created but formatting doesn't render (shows as plain text)' — i.e. ADF JSON on the create surface is stored literally as text.

Repo contrast: descriptions send ADF as a REST payload/JSON field (acli_cli_ops.py:385 `payload['description'] = _text_to_adf(...)`; acli.py:209 `--description json.dumps(_text_to_adf(...))`), a different mechanism than the comment `--body <str>` flag the plan reuses, so the 'like --description' analogy does not establish inline --body ADF rendering.
findings.finding: The load-bearing claim that `acli jira workitem comment create --body json.dumps(to_wire(fitted))` renders as ADF is unverified against prior art and is contradicted by retrieved sources; the --help string only shows the flag ACCEPTS an ADF-shaped string, not that Jira RENDERS the inline JSON as formatted ADF on the create surface.
findings.location: Approach 2 / '--body accepts ADF, and fit BEFORE encode (Cloud, load-bearing)'; acli_cli_ops.py add_comment (:492-529)
scenarios: rich_text_cutover flips 'cloud' on; Cloud comment create sends json.dumps(to_wire(fitted)) via --body and the JSON string is posted verbatim as the comment text instead of formatted ADF.
A32a _resolve_codec is flipped to the real codec so the local dedup key equals the rendered wire, but the landed comment body is the raw JSON string, so subsequent diffs may not converge as intended.
findings.suggested_fix: Probe the actual rendered result (create a throwaway comment in a scratch issue and read it back, or dry-run the REST payload) to confirm ADF rendering on create; if inline --body does not render, switch the Cloud create path to the documented `--body-adf <file>` (writing the ADF JSON to a temp file) or to a REST comment payload mirroring the description path, and update the plan's capability claim and probe basis accordingly.
